categories.main_business_segments: Nutanix operates as a single reportable segment focused on providing the Nutanix Cloud Platform, an enterprise cloud software platform. The platform encompasses core offerings in cloud infrastructure (hyperconverged infrastructure, virtualization, storage, networking), cloud management, unified storage, and database services, delivered as software and cloud services for hybrid and multicloud environments.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Nutanix pioneered hyperconverged infrastructure (HCI), integrating compute, storage, and networking into a single software stack (AOS) with a native hypervisor (AHV) based on KVM. The platform is built on web-scale engineering principles, emphasizing automation, operational simplicity, and scalability. Nutanix software is hardware-agnostic, running on qualified servers from OEM partners or in public clouds, and includes advanced data services, virtual networking, Kubernetes management, and cloud-based SaaS offerings.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Nutanix serves a broad and diverse customer base of over 24,000 end customers, including approximately 1,020 Global 2000 enterprises. Its solutions are used across industries such as automotive, consumer goods, education, energy, financial services, healthcare, manufacturing, media, public sector, retail, technology, and telecommunications. Customers include enterprises, service providers, and government entities seeking to modernize IT infrastructure and manage hybrid/multicloud workloads.
categories.geographic_coverage: Nutanix operates globally, with significant revenue from the United States (about 56% in FY23), and the remainder from Europe, the Middle East, Africa, Asia Pacific, and the Americas. The company maintains offices and R&D centers across North America, Europe, Asia Pacific, the Middle East, Latin America, and Africa, and derives approximately 44% of its revenue from international customers.
categories.supply_chain_position: Nutanix is positioned as a software and cloud platform provider (downstream in the IT supply chain), enabling customers to build and operate private, hybrid, and multicloud environments. While it does not manufacture hardware, it partners with OEMs and contract manufacturers for hardware appliances, and relies on channel partners and OEMs for distribution and fulfillment.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Nutanix's strategic focus is on continued innovation in hybrid and multicloud infrastructure, automation, and operational simplicity. R&D investments target expanding platform capabilities (including AI/ML workloads, Kubernetes, cloud management, and data services), deepening integration with ecosystem partners, and enhancing user experience. The company is also investing in AI capabilities and transitioning to a subscription-based business model to drive recurring revenue and customer retention.
categories.revenue_model: Nutanix generates revenue primarily through subscription-based software licenses, support and entitlement subscriptions, and cloud-based SaaS offerings, with terms typically ranging from one to five years. Revenue is recognized both upfront (for certain licenses) and ratably (for subscriptions and SaaS). The company also derives revenue from professional services and, to a lesser extent, hardware sales through OEM and channel partners.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Nutanix competes in the highly competitive enterprise IT infrastructure market against software providers like VMware, public cloud providers (AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle Cloud), and traditional IT systems vendors (Dell, HPE, IBM, Lenovo, NetApp, Pure Storage, Huawei). Nutanix is recognized as a pioneer and leader in HCI and is positioning itself as a leading platform for hybrid and multicloud environments, emphasizing openness, simplicity, and customer choice.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ended July 31, 2023, Nutanix reported total revenue of $1.86 billion, with subscription revenue accounting for 93% of total billings and $1.7 billion in subscription revenue (up 21% year-over-year). The company had over 24,000 end customers and approximately 6,450 employees. Nutanix has a history of GAAP net losses but achieved non-GAAP profitability in FY23, with a focus on improving operating cash flow and sustaining profitable growth.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Nutanix delivers a unified, open, and simple cloud platform that enables organizations to seamlessly run and manage applications and data across private, hybrid, and multicloud environments. Its differentiation lies in operational simplicity, scalability, hardware and cloud flexibility, integrated data services, and a consistent operating model. Nutanix emphasizes customer choice, rapid innovation, and a strong ecosystem, aiming to reduce IT complexity and total cost of ownership for its customers.
